title: Light intensity as a limiting factor
caption: At low light intensity the rate rises in proportion to the light, whatever the CO₂ concentration or temperature: light is the limiting factor. At high intensity the curve levels off, and a higher CO₂ concentration (or temperature) lifts the plateau, because a different factor is now limiting.
alt: Two curves of photosynthesis rate against light intensity that rise together and then level off: a lower plateau at low CO2 and a higher plateau at high CO2.
description: At low light intensity both curves rise together: light is limiting.
At high light intensity each curve levels off: another factor, such as CO₂ or temperature, is now limiting.
With more CO₂ the plateau is higher (100 against 50).
Glasshouses raise light, CO₂ and temperature to raise yields.
